newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Dec 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Dec 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Sports Commission announced yesterday that athletics, the banner sport of the Olympics, will suffer severely as money is redirected towards sports Australia is most likely to win medals in during the year 2000. Athletics Australia has warned it will use every means at its disposal to make up the shortfall in Government funding from the corporate sector. Page 36.

Australia's most prestigious sports awards, the Telstra-sponsored Confederation of Australian Sport awards, may be disrupted by an ongoing legal dispute between Olympic gold-medallist Kieren Perkins and Telstra. It is expected Perkins will refuse a nomination for the awards, and his management company has advised Kieren to avoid any association with the telecommunications giant until the dispute is resolved. Page 36.

The Australian cricket side is revamping itself in an attempt to become more aggressive, after losing seven straight one-day matches played in Sri Lanka and India. Part of this revamping is the surprise inclusion of Tom Moody into the one-day team. Page 36.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A fast-paced new craze is hitting the streets - Street hockey. Originally developed in an attempt to adapt ice hockey to a warmer climate, it is now being played in over 140 countries worldwide. Page 41.

Victorian golfer Mark Allen took a one-stroke lead yesterday at the New Zealand Open, after playing the best round of his professional career. A succession of long putts early in his round saw him one shot clear of the favourite, New Zealand's Michael Lang. Page 41.

The Gippsland Falcons, previously expected to come last in the national soccer competition, are now poised to reap the rewards of gaining former Australian international Eddie Krncevic as their coach. The benefits are already showing, with three goals scored in the past two weeks, and the achievement of a mid-table position. Page 41.
THE AGE

Under a proposal by the Teletrak company, proprietary racing may secure a foothold. According to Teletrak, a provisional agreement with the Australian Quarter-Horse Racing Association was entered into last week, promising the staging of seven races each Monday night at the Calder Park Thunderdome. Page C8.

Cricketer Matthew Elliott has set his sights on playing for Victoria in a Mercantile Mutual Cup one-day game in January, despite medical opinions that say his knee injury will keep him out of competition for eight to 12 weeks. Elliott underwent surgery on Tuesday to re-attach cartilage to the bone of his right knee. Page C8.

Hawthorn chief executive Morton Browne will announce at the Hawk's annual meeting on Monday a loss of A$1.1 million. The figure is A$200,000 worse than was predicted by the former board in the lead-up to the failed Melbourne merger. Page C8.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian basketballers Ranae Fergent and Natasha O'Brien, currently attending the University of Oregon, have been found to have breached United States college basketball rules by playing in the Australian Women's National Basketball League, resulting in the suspension of both players. Page 101.

According to Australian men's hockey coach Barry Dancer, the Kookaburras' sweep of the three-game series against India yesterday has gained invaluable experience and confidence for the team. The Kookaburras thrashed India in a 5-2 match, completing their preparation for the six-nation Champions Trophy Tournament, starting tomorrow in India. Page 103.

Australian tennis player Mark Woodforde has beaten the world's number one, Andre Agassi, during the Grand Slam Cup in Munich yesterday. The win has secured a place in the event's quarter-finals for Woodforde, and guaranteed him at least A$322,000 in prizmoney. Page 103.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Six-year old gelding Magic Road gave veteran trainer Col Harwood back-to-back wins in the A$150,000 Panthers Hawkesbury Gold Cup yesterday at Hawkesbury. Harwood, the victim of a severe stroke in 1991, was swamped by family and well-wishers offering congatulations. Page 100.

Soccer has secured a A$2.3 million, three-year budget as part of the Australian Institute of Sport program, despite the defection of Joe Simunic to Croatia. The funding program, announced yesterday, revealed major cuts for several sports and it was feared Soccer would suffer the same fate. Page 102.

Complications from a recent brain tumour operation saw champion jockey Wayne Harris rushed to hospital in a critical condition earlier this week. Harris has been fighting to overcome meningitis since the removal of the tumour, and is due to undergo majorsurgery this morning. Page 107.
